gloss: one bad thing after another; adding insult to injury

definitions.gloss: one bad thing after another; adding insult to injury
definitions.explanation: Literally being trampled and then kicked: suffering one blow after another, or being treated badly on top of an earlier misfortune. Used as a predicate with だ or before a noun with の.

examples.japanese: ⟦{今日|きょう}→今日：00496_kyou⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{踏|ふ}んだり{蹴|け}ったりだ。
examples.english: Today has been one thing after another.

examples.japanese: ⟦{雨|あめ}→雨：00583_ame⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{降|ふ}られて→降る：00839_furu⟧⟦{電車|でんしゃ}→電車：00522_densha⟧⟦も→も：00484_mo⟧⟦{遅|おく}れ→遅れる：00741_okureru⟧、{踏|ふ}んだり{蹴|け}ったり⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{一日|いちにち}→一日：00942_ichinichi⟧だった。
examples.english: I got caught in the rain and the train was late too; everything went wrong all day.

examples.japanese: ⟦{振|ふ}られた→振る：01983_furu⟧うえ⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{貸|か}した→貸す：00537_kasu⟧⟦お{金|かね}→お金：00611_okane⟧⟦も→も：00484_mo⟧⟦{返|かえ}って→返る：29164_kaeru⟧こない⟦なんて→なんて：06918_nante⟧、{踏|ふ}んだり{蹴|け}ったりだ⟦よ→よ：09475_yo⟧。
examples.english: She dumped me and I won't get back the money I lent her either. Talk about adding insult to injury.

notes:
COMMON PATTERNS:
- {踏|ふ}んだり{蹴|け}ったりだ: it's one blow after another
- {踏|ふ}んだり{蹴|け}ったり⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{一日|いちにち}→一日：00942_ichinichi⟧: a day when everything went wrong
- {踏|ふ}んだり{蹴|け}ったりな⟦{目|め}に{遭|あ}う→目に遭う：25927_meniau⟧: to be hit by one misfortune after another

USAGE:
Conversational. Often a complaint about how one was treated by others, not only about bad luck.

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦{弱|よわ}り{目|め}に{祟|たた}り{目|め}→弱り目に祟り目：31638_yowarimenitatarime⟧: a proverb with the same idea, more bookish
- ⟦{泣|な}きっ{面|つら}に{蜂|はち}→泣きっ面に蜂：31604_nakittsuranihachi⟧: a bee stinging a crying face
